learning_outcomes.text: Generic knowledge of Manufacturing Engineering, manufacturing processes, and their place in the productive context.
Ability to identify different manufacturing processes and their characteristics for classification.
Knowledge of the main production systems and the automation of machine tools using numerical control techniques.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of quality and the implementation of standardized quality systems in production processes.
Ability to analyze and assess the environmental impact of possible technical solutions linked to manufacturing or production processes.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary and multilingual environment.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction to Manufacturing Processes: Basic concepts. Types of manufacturing processes.
Topic 5. Welding processes and other joining and assembly processes.
Topic 6. New technologies in processes, machine tools, and manufacturing equipment.
Topic 7. Automation of manufacturing processes. Numerical control.
Topic 8. Dimensional metrology. Instrumentation and measurement techniques.
Topic 9. Manufacturing in a competitive environment. Flexible manufacturing systems.
Topic 10. Automated manufacturing and assembly systems applied to the renewable energy industry.
MODULE II: QUALITY ENGINEERING IN MANUFACTURING SYSTEMS
Topic 11. Quality and quality control in manufacturing.
Topic 12. Organization and quality management in manufacturing systems.
Topic 13. Methods study and time control.
MODULE III: ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING: ENVIRONMENTAL TECHNOLOGIES AND ENERGY MANAGEMENT
Topic 14. Pollution and Environmental Technologies for energy saving and waste prevention. Sustainability.
Topic 15. Environmental management systems and audits (EMAS) for manufacturing systems.
teaching_methods: Use of audiovisual media and digital presentations
Use of the Wooclap online platform for real-time interaction and online tests
Coordination of visits to industries and places of interest
assessment_rules: The evaluation follows continuous assessment, unless a student opts for a single assessment (100% final exam) before 40% of continuous assessment activities occur. The final grade is obtained from the weighted average (40% 1st partial, 40% 2nd partial, 20% assignments/projects), provided a minimum of 5 points (out of 10) is obtained in each partial exam. Failed partials can be recovered in the first official call; if both are failed, the student must retake the entire subject in the second call. The assignments/projects block is not recoverable, but if a student has passed both partials and still fails, a specific exam on activities/tasks/projects can be taken in official calls.
